class.name: JSBSimAutopilot
class.brief_description: An autopilot for a [JSBSimAircraft]: heading, altitude and airspeed holds and waypoint routes.
class.description: Add it as a child of a [JSBSimAircraft]; it works with any JSBSim model and needs nothing in the aircraft's XML. The aircraft calls it before every JSBSim step (at [member JSBSimAircraft.rate], independent of the frame rate) and the autopilot writes the aircraft's pilot commands [member JSBSimAircraft.aileron], [member JSBSimAircraft.elevator] and [member JSBSimAircraft.rudder], and [member JSBSimAircraft.throttle] if [member speed_hold] is on. If the parent is not a [JSBSimAircraft] a warning is printed and the node does nothing. While [member enabled] is [code]true[/code] the autopilot always flies the stick and pedals, so manual input to those commands is overwritten. Without any mode it keeps the wings level and flies [member target_vertical_speed]. The modes add to that: [member heading_hold] turns to [member target_heading], [member follow_route] flies the waypoints, [member altitude_hold] climbs or descends to [member target_altitude] and [member speed_hold] holds [member target_speed] with the throttle. Without [member speed_hold] the throttle stays with the pilot. The loops are cascaded PID controllers on JSBSim's own state: heading or route track to bank to aileron, sideslip to rudder, height to vertical speed to pitch to elevator, and airspeed to throttle. A loop that was off starts from the current command, so switching on does not jump. The defaults suit the bundled J3Cub; the properties in the [b]Tuning[/b] group are for other aircraft. Units: angles in degrees, heights in metres above the WGS84 ellipsoid (like [member JSBSimAircraft.height]), distances in metres, airspeeds in calibrated knots, vertical speeds in m/s. [codeblock] var autopilot := JSBSimAutopilot.new() aircraft.add_child(autopilot) # aircraft: a JSBSimAircraft autopilot.add_waypoint(41.05, 29.10, 900.0, 70.0) # latitude, longitude, height (m), speed (kt) autopilot.add_waypoint(41.10, 29.20) # keeps the current height and speed targets autopilot.add_waypoint_local(Vector3(2000.0, 900.0, -3000.0)) # a scene position; y is the height autopilot.loop_route = true autopilot.altitude_hold = true autopilot.speed_hold = true autopilot.follow_route = true autopilot.enabled = true autopilot.waypoint_reached.connect(func(index): print("reached ", index)) [/codeblock] [method engage] turns the autopilot on holding the current heading, height and airspeed.

method.name: add_waypoint
method.description: Appends a waypoint to the route. [param latitude] and [param longitude] are geodetic degrees. [param height] is metres above the WGS84 ellipsoid and [param speed] is calibrated knots; if either is [code]NAN[/code] (the default) the corresponding target ([member target_altitude], [member target_speed]) is not changed when the waypoint becomes active. A waypoint with a height or speed sets the target when it becomes the active one; it takes effect while [member altitude_hold] or [member speed_hold] is on. The first waypoint added to an empty route becomes active immediately. Adding waypoints does not turn on [member follow_route] or [member enabled]. A latitude or longitude that is not finite, or a latitude beyond 90 degrees, pushes an error and the waypoint is not added.

method.name: add_waypoint_local
method.description: Appends a waypoint at the scene position [param position] of the parent aircraft's frame (+X east, +Y up, -Z north, metres); its y is the waypoint's height. [param speed] is as in [method add_waypoint]. The position is converted to latitude, longitude and ellipsoid height. Pushes an error and adds nothing if the parent aircraft has not started ([method JSBSimAircraft.start]), since the frame is not known before.

method.name: clear_route
method.description: Removes all waypoints. There is no active waypoint afterwards ([method get_active_waypoint] returns -1). [member follow_route] is not changed; with an empty route the autopilot falls back to [member heading_hold] or wings level.

method.name: engage
method.description: Turns the autopilot on holding the current state: [member target_heading], [member target_altitude] and [member target_speed] are set to the aircraft's present true heading, ellipsoid height and calibrated airspeed, and [member heading_hold], [member altitude_hold], [member speed_hold] and [member enabled] are set. [member follow_route] is not changed. Pushes an error if the parent aircraft has not started.

method.name: get_active_waypoint
method.description: Returns the index of the waypoint being flown to, or -1 if there is no route or the end of a route without [member loop_route] was passed.

method.name: get_commanded_bank
method.description: Returns the bank angle in degrees the autopilot last commanded (positive is right bank), limited to [member max_bank]. Updated while [member enabled].

method.name: get_commanded_pitch
method.description: Returns the pitch angle in degrees the autopilot last commanded, limited to [member min_pitch] and [member max_pitch]. Updated while [member enabled].

method.name: get_commanded_vertical_speed
method.description: Returns the vertical speed in m/s (positive is up) the autopilot last commanded, after the climb and descent limits and the airspeed protection. Updated while [member enabled].

method.name: get_cross_track_error
method.description: Returns the distance in metres of the aircraft from the active leg, positive to the right of the leg. Valid while [member follow_route] flies a route.

method.name: get_desired_track
method.description: Returns the ground track in degrees true (0..360) the autopilot is steering for on the active leg, including the correction toward the leg. Valid while [member follow_route] flies a route.

method.name: get_distance_to_waypoint
method.description: Returns the horizontal distance in metres to the active waypoint. Valid while [member follow_route] flies a route.

method.name: get_waypoint
method.description: Returns waypoint [param index] as a [Dictionary] with the keys [code]latitude[/code] and [code]longitude[/code] (degrees), [code]height[/code] (metres, [code]NAN[/code] if the waypoint has none), [code]speed[/code] (knots, [code]NAN[/code] if none) and, if the parent aircraft has started, [code]position[/code] (a [Vector3] in the aircraft's scene frame; a waypoint without a height is placed at the height of the frame's origin). Returns an empty dictionary and pushes an error if [param index] is out of range.

method.name: get_waypoint_count
method.description: Returns the number of waypoints in the route.

method.name: set_active_waypoint
method.description: Makes waypoint [param index] the one flown to, on a leg that starts at the aircraft's position at the next update, and applies its height and speed targets. Use it to skip ahead or to restart a route that has finished (also set [member follow_route] again in that case). Pushes an error if [param index] is out of range.

method.name: update
method.description: Computes the commands for one JSBSim step of [param dt] seconds and writes them to the parent aircraft. Does nothing unless [member enabled]. [JSBSimAircraft] calls it before every step; you normally do not need to.

members.member: Gain of the height loop: commanded climb in m/s per metre of height error (before the limits [member max_climb_rate] and [member max_descent_rate]).
If [code]true[/code], the autopilot climbs or descends to [member target_altitude]. If [code]false[/code] it flies [member target_vertical_speed].

Distance in metres from a waypoint at which it counts as reached. A waypoint is also reached earlier, when a turn to the next leg has to start (turn anticipation), or when the aircraft passes the end of the leg.

Master switch. If [code]true[/code] the autopilot writes the aileron, elevator and rudder commands of the aircraft before every step (and the throttle if [member speed_hold] is on). With no other mode it keeps the wings level and flies [member target_vertical_speed]. If [code]false[/code] it writes nothing. The loops start from the current commands when this is turned on.

If [code]true[/code] and [member enabled], the autopilot flies the route instead of [member target_heading]: it follows the ground track of each leg (so a crosswind is corrected) and returns to the leg at up to [member max_intercept] degrees. When the last waypoint of a route without [member loop_route] is reached, [signal route_finished] is emitted, this property is set to [code]false[/code], [member heading_hold] is set to [code]true[/code] and [member target_heading] to the course of the last leg. Without an active waypoint the autopilot uses [member heading_hold].
Gain of the heading loop: degrees of commanded bank per degree of heading error.
If [code]true[/code], the autopilot turns to [member target_heading] (bank limited to [member max_bank]). Used when no route is flown; [member follow_route] takes precedence while a route is active.
If [code]true[/code], the route continues with the first waypoint after the last one. A loop needs at least two waypoints; a single waypoint is reached once.
Limit of the commanded bank angle in degrees. Turn anticipation also assumes 80 % of it.
Limit of the commanded climb rate in m/s. Set it to what the aircraft can climb at full power.
Limit of the commanded descent rate in m/s, as a positive number.
Maximum angle in degrees between the commanded track and the leg while returning to the leg.
Upper limit of the commanded pitch angle in degrees.
Upper limit of the throttle set by [member speed_hold].

Calibrated airspeed in knots below which the autopilot gives up height to regain speed. The climb command is reduced from 10 kt above this speed, and below it a descent proportional to the deficit is commanded. Set it a little above the aircraft's stall speed.
Lower limit of the commanded pitch angle in degrees (a negative number).
Lower limit of the throttle set by [member speed_hold].
Damping of the pitch loop: elevator per degree per second of pitch rate.
Integral gain of the pitch loop: elevator per degree of pitch error per second. The integral is limited.
Proportional gain of the pitch loop: elevator command per degree of pitch error.
Damping of the roll loop: aileron per degree per second of roll rate.
Integral gain of the roll loop: aileron per degree of bank error per second. The integral is limited.
Proportional gain of the roll loop: aileron command per degree of bank error.
If [code]true[/code], the autopilot sets the throttle to hold [member target_speed], between [member min_throttle] and [member max_throttle]. If [code]false[/code] the throttle is left to the pilot.
Integral gain of the speed loop: throttle per knot of airspeed error per second. The integral is limited by the throttle limits.
Proportional gain of the speed loop: throttle per knot of airspeed error.
Height in metres above the WGS84 ellipsoid held while [member altitude_hold] is on. Waypoints with a height set it when they become active.
True heading in degrees held while [member heading_hold] is on and no route is flown.
Calibrated airspeed in knots held while [member speed_hold] is on. Waypoints with a speed set it when they become active.
Vertical speed in m/s (positive is up) flown while [member altitude_hold] is off, subject to the climb and descent limits.
Gain of the route loop: degrees of commanded bank per degree of ground track error.
Distance in metres ahead on the leg the aircraft steers toward when returning to it. A larger value returns to the leg more gently; about ten seconds of ground speed is a good start.
Integral gain of the vertical speed loop: degrees of pitch per m/s of vertical speed error per second.
Gain of the vertical speed loop: degrees of commanded pitch per m/s of vertical speed error.
Gain of the turn coordination: rudder command per degree of sideslip (positive sideslip gives right pedal). The rudder is always driven while [member enabled].

signal.name: route_finished
signal.description: Emitted after the last waypoint of a route without [member loop_route] was reached (and after its [signal waypoint_reached]). The autopilot then keeps the last leg's course with [member heading_hold]. A route of a single waypoint also finishes, even with [member loop_route].

signal.name: waypoint_reached
signal.description: Emitted when waypoint [param index] counts as reached: within [member capture_radius] or the turn anticipation distance, or past the end of the leg. The autopilot then continues with the next waypoint (the first one after the last, with [member loop_route]).
